cards.name: High Availability Architecture
cards.az900ExamTip: HA ensures service uptime through redundancy and automated failover across fault domains
cards.description: Design pattern for minimizing downtime through redundant components and health probes

cards.name: Elastic Scaling
cards.az900ExamTip: Elasticity allows resources to dynamically allocate and deallocate based on fluctuating demand
cards.description: Automatic resource adjustment to match demand without over-provisioning

cards.name: OpEx Advantage
cards.az900ExamTip: OpEx shifts upfront CapEx into ongoing operational expense with pay-as-you-go billing
cards.description: Operational expenditure model enabling agile cloud cost management without initial hardware outlays

cards.name: CapEx Planning
cards.az900ExamTip: CapEx involves upfront spending on physical infrastructure deducted over its lifecycle
cards.description: Capital expenditure planning relevant when comparing on-premises TCO with cloud migration

cards.name: Vertical Scaling (Scale Up)
cards.az900ExamTip: Scale up adds CPU or RAM to an existing virtual machine or service instance
cards.description: Increasing the processing power and memory capacity of existing resources

cards.name: Horizontal Scaling (Scale Out)
cards.az900ExamTip: Scale out adds more virtual machines or service instances to share the workload
cards.description: Adding additional identical instances behind load balancers for parallel throughput

cards.name: Cloud Agility
cards.az900ExamTip: Agility describes the rapid provisioning and deployment of software and cloud resources
cards.description: Accelerating time-to-market by spinning up dev/test environments in minutes

cards.name: Disaster Recovery Planning
cards.az900ExamTip: DR focuses on restoring services after catastrophic failures using paired regions and backups
cards.description: Structured architecture for RTO and RPO business continuity across geographical regions

cards.name: Fault Tolerance Design
cards.az900ExamTip: Fault tolerance guarantees zero downtime by operating redundant hardware concurrently
cards.description: Ensuring continuous operation without human intervention when hardware components fail

cards.name: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
cards.az900ExamTip: IaaS provides raw compute/network/storage where the customer manages OS and software
cards.description: Maximum architectural control with customer responsibility for OS updates and patching

cards.name: Platform as a Service (PaaS)
cards.az900ExamTip: PaaS handles OS, runtime, and patching so developers focus strictly on application code
cards.description: Managed application platform delivering developer velocity without infrastructure toil

cards.name: Software as a Service (SaaS)
cards.az900ExamTip: SaaS delivers end-user software hosted and managed completely by the cloud vendor (e.g. M365)
cards.description: Complete cloud application consumed on a subscription basis with minimal administration

cards.name: Public Cloud Deployment
cards.az900ExamTip: Public cloud infrastructure is owned by the provider and shared across multiple tenants securely
cards.description: Standard multi-tenant public infrastructure with near-infinite on-demand elasticity

cards.name: Private Cloud Infrastructure
cards.az900ExamTip: Private cloud is dedicated to a single organization, either on-premise or hosted by third-party
cards.description: Dedicated single-tenant infrastructure providing full control and isolation

cards.name: Hybrid Cloud Architecture
cards.az900ExamTip: Hybrid cloud connects on-premises datacenters with public cloud environments securely
cards.description: Seamless integration of on-premises workloads with Azure for burst capacity and migration

cards.name: Shared Responsibility Model
cards.az900ExamTip: Customer is always responsible for data and identity; provider responsibility increases from IaaS to SaaS
cards.description: Defines security and operational boundaries between customer and Microsoft across service models

cards.name: Consumption-Based Pricing
cards.az900ExamTip: In a consumption model, you pay only for resources actively used with zero idle cost
cards.description: Pay-for-what-you-use billing ideal for sporadic workloads and serverless executions

cards.name: Economies of Scale
cards.az900ExamTip: Cloud providers pass hardware volume purchasing savings directly to customers as lower unit prices
cards.description: Leveraging hyper-scale provider infrastructure to achieve lower per-unit computing costs
